name: phase0_warmup_check
description: Does --warmup-blocks remove the run-level startup transient that --settle
cannot?
ws_init mmaps WS_SLOTS x working-set bytes per thread under MAP_POPULATE,
and ws_get fills a slot the first time a selector selects it. For a
4-thread ws_dram_x8 run that is 256 MB faulted in and 128 MB written
before the second condition is ever measured. In
results/20260822-234811-phase1_traffic_volume that showed as +2.75 W across
the first ~4 blocks, and moved that run's A/A estimate anywhere from +8 to
-37 mW depending on how many blocks were dropped after the fact. --settle
discards samples within a block, so it is no defence.
Both arms are A/A, so any difference between the first blocks and the run's
steady state is transient and nothing else. The warmup arm cycles through
both conditions before recording, which also forces ws_get to fill every
slot up front.
Second purpose: these are six more ws_dram_x8 A/A repeats, against the
unexplained +15.4 mW cond-1 offset that victim showed in the sweep. The
polarity control established the measurement path carries no such bias
(B = +0.7 +/- 3.1 mW over eight ws_l3_x8 A/A runs), so if the offset is
real it is specific to this victim or that session and should show here.
Driver settings match phase1_traffic_volume and phase1_polarity so the
numbers are directly comparable; the seed differs again.

runs.label: dram_aa_nowarm
runs.comment: Current behaviour. The transient, if present, lands in block 0.

runs.label: dram_aa_warm
